questions.question_text: A WV salesperson is asked to prepare a deed for a client. Can the salesperson legally do this?
questions.correct_answer: No, that constitutes unauthorized practice of law
distractors: Yes, if the broker approves
Yes, for standard residential transactions
Yes, with a disclaimer that it is not legal advice
questions.explanation: Licensees may fill in blanks on approved forms but may not draft legal documents or give legal advice. Preparing a deed is the practice of law and requires an attorney.

questions.question_text: Which of the following activities is within a WV licensee's scope of practice?
questions.correct_answer: Filling in the blanks on a standard contract form at the parties' direction
distractors: Drafting a custom purchase agreement
Giving legal advice on title issues
Rendering an opinion on whether a clause is enforceable
questions.explanation: Completing the blanks on a standard form at the parties' direction is ordinary brokerage work; drafting legal documents, giving legal advice and opining on enforceability are not. §30-40-19(a)(21) makes it a disciplinary ground to engage in "the unlawful or unauthorized practice of law as defined by the Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia" — so the boundary is set by the Court, not by the Commission. Note that the WVREC promulgates only the Notice of Agency Relationship form; it has not adopted or approved standard purchase contracts.

questions.question_text: A buyer asks their WV salesperson whether a contract clause will hold up in court. How should the salesperson respond?
questions.correct_answer: Advise the buyer to consult an attorney of their own choosing
distractors: Provide their professional legal opinion
Assure the buyer the clause is enforceable
Recommend a specific attorney the brokerage works with
questions.explanation: Opining on whether a clause will hold up in court is the unauthorized practice of law (§30-40-19(a)(21)). The right move is to tell the buyer to consult an attorney of the buyer's own choosing. Be careful about naming one: §30-40-19(a)(20) makes it a disciplinary ground to "procure an attorney for any client or customer, or solicit legal business for any attorney-at-law."

questions.question_text: A WV salesperson with a broker license works as an associate broker. What type of activities can they perform?
distractors: All broker-level activities done independently
Only listing and selling residential properties
Only activities pre-approved by their clients
questions.explanation: An associate broker works under another broker's supervision and operates within the scope of their license type, similar to a salesperson despite holding broker qualifications.

questions.question_text: A WV licensee is helping a client complete a standard purchase contract. Which of these is safely within the licensee's scope?
questions.correct_answer: Filling in the blanks to record what the parties have agreed
distractors: Drafting new clauses to address a novel legal issue
Advising the client on the legal effect of a clause
Preparing the deed that will convey the property
questions.explanation: Recording the parties' agreement in the blanks is within scope, and §30-40-26(f) in fact requires the licensee to "make certain that all the terms and conditions of a real estate transaction are contained in any contract prepared by the licensee." Drafting new legal clauses, advising on legal effect, and preparing deeds are the practice of law, which §30-40-19(a)(21) defines by reference to the Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia.

questions.question_text: In West Virginia, how are real estate commission rates determined?
distractors: Set by the WVREC at a fixed percentage
Determined by the local Board of REALTORS
Fixed at 6% by state law
questions.explanation: Commission compensation in WV is negotiable — there are no fixed fee schedules. Setting uniform commission rates would violate antitrust laws.

questions.question_text: A client wants to pay their WV salesperson directly for helping sell a property. Is this permitted?
questions.correct_answer: No, all compensation must go through the broker
distractors: Yes, direct payment is always permitted
Yes, if both parties sign a written agreement
Yes, for transactions under $50,000
questions.explanation: §30-40-19(a)(16) makes it a disciplinary ground for a salesperson or associate broker to accept compensation for any act under the article "from any person other than his or her broker," and 174-1-15.2 bars collecting any money in a transaction except in the name of and with the consent of the responsible broker. One wrinkle: under the §30-40-4 definition of "salesperson," a salesperson may designate an entity such as an LLC or S-corporation to receive the compensation payable to them — but the broker is still the one paying it.

questions.question_text: Under §30-40-26, what must every contract in which a WV broker is obligated to represent a principal contain?
distractors: A state-mandated minimum commission
An automatic renewal unless the principal cancels
The broker's profit margin breakdown
questions.explanation: §30-40-26(b) requires every representation contract to contain a definite expiration date and forbids any provision requiring the principal to notify the broker of an intent to cancel after that date — so automatic renewals are out. §30-40-26(c) bars any provision obligating the signer to pay the broker after expiration if they then sign with a different broker, and §30-40-26(a),(g),(h) require a true legible copy to every person who signs.

questions.question_text: Are net listings prohibited in West Virginia?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, they are prohibited under WV law
distractors: No, they are not specifically prohibited but raise conflict concerns
No, they are encouraged for transparency
Only prohibited for residential properties
questions.explanation: West Virginia prohibits net listings by name. §30-40-19(a)(40) makes it a ground for refusal, suspension, revocation or other sanction to "obtain, negotiate, or attempt to obtain or negotiate a contract whereby the broker is entitled to a commission only to the extent that the sales price exceeds a given amount, commonly referred to as a net listing."

questions.question_text: A seller offers to pay the salesperson a bonus directly for a quick sale. What should the salesperson do?
questions.correct_answer: Decline and route the bonus through the broker
distractors: Accept the bonus as a personal gift from seller
Accept the payment if the amount is under $500
Report the bonus offer to the WVREC immediately
questions.explanation: Accepting the bonus directly would violate §30-40-19(a)(16), and 174-1-15.2 forbids a salesperson from collecting any money in connection with a real estate transaction — "whether as a commission, deposit, payment, rental, or otherwise" — except in the name of and with the consent of the responsible broker. Route it through the broker.

questions.question_text: West Virginia follows which legal doctrine regarding seller disclosure of property conditions?
distractors: Full mandatory disclosure
Caveat venditor (seller beware)
Strict liability for defects
questions.explanation: WV follows caveat emptor more strictly than most states. Sellers are generally not required to volunteer property condition information, but may not actively conceal known defects.

questions.question_text: A WV seller knows the basement floods during heavy rain but does not mention it to the buyer. Is this legal?
questions.correct_answer: No, active concealment of known defects is prohibited
distractors: Yes, caveat emptor means no duty to disclose
Yes, unless the buyer specifically asks
Only illegal if the seller signed a disclosure form
questions.explanation: Caveat emptor limits the duty to volunteer information, but it does not license concealment. For a licensee, §30-40-19(a)(22) makes it a disciplinary ground to commit or be a party to "any material fraud, misrepresentation, concealment, conspiracy, collusion, trick, scheme, or other device whereby any other person relies upon the word, representation, or conduct of the licensee." A seller who hides a known flooding problem faces common-law fraud exposure on the same reasoning.

questions.question_text: Does West Virginia require sellers to complete a standardized property condition disclosure form?
questions.correct_answer: No, WV has no mandatory disclosure form
distractors: Yes, similar to California's TDS
Yes, for properties built before 1978
Yes, but only for properties over $100,000
questions.explanation: WV does not have a mandatory standardized seller disclosure form equivalent to states like California. However, the federal lead-based paint disclosure still applies for pre-1978 homes.

questions.question_text: A WV listing agent knows a property has termite damage but the seller instructs them not to disclose it. What should the agent do?
questions.correct_answer: Disclose the material fact to all parties
distractors: Follow the seller's instructions to remain silent
Only disclose if the buyer's agent asks
Withdraw from the listing immediately
questions.explanation: A licensee cannot follow an instruction to conceal. §30-40-19(a)(22) reaches material fraud, misrepresentation and concealment, and (a)(37) reaches any conduct demonstrating bad faith or dishonest, fraudulent or improper dealing. The WVREC's Notice of Agency Relationship also commits every licensee to "a duty of honest and fair dealing and good faith" toward all consumers, whether or not they are clients.

questions.question_text: Under WV's caveat emptor framework, what should agents recommend to buyers?
distractors: Rely on the seller's verbal assurances
Skip inspections to save money
Trust the property's age as an indicator
questions.explanation: Because WV follows caveat emptor with no mandatory seller disclosure form, agents should recommend that buyers obtain professional inspections to protect themselves.
